title: Session Musician and Vocalist Release
summary: Pay a session player or background vocalist a flat fee and get the rights to their recorded performance.
useWhen: Hiring instrumentalists or background vocalists for a recording session.
watchOuts: Under U.S. copyright law, a work by a non-employee is a 'work made for hire' only if it falls within one of nine statutory categories (such as a contribution to a collective work or part of an audiovisual work) and the parties sign a written agreement saying so. A stand-alone sound recording or beat is often not in those categories, which is why this template also includes a written assignment.
Union members (AFM for musicians, SAG-AFTRA for vocalists) work under collective bargaining agreements with minimum scale, pension and new-use payments. A private release cannot override them.

Non-featured musicians and vocalists receive a statutory share of SoundExchange royalties through the AFM & SAG-AFTRA Intellectual Property Rights Distribution Fund. That is set by law (17 U.S.C. §114(g)(2)) and not affected by this release.
If a session player contributes to the songwriting (melody, lyrics or distinctive parts), they may be a co-writer. Use a split sheet if so.

California: commissioning a 'work made for hire' from an individual can make the commissioning party that individual's employer for workers' compensation and unemployment insurance purposes (Cal. Labor Code §3351.5(c), Unemployment Insurance Code §686). Many California deals use an assignment instead of work-for-hire language.

variables.label: Did the performer contribute to the songwriting?
variables.help: If yes, use a split sheet.

variables.label: Governing law (state)
variables.help: Two-letter code of the state whose law governs this agreement. Usually where the parties or the work are located.

sections.title: 1. Session
sections.body:
{{musician_name}} ("Performer", {{musician_email}}), credited as {{musician_alias}}, will perform {{instrument}} on the following songs for {{producer_name}} ("Owner") on {{session_date}}:

{{songs}}

sections.title: 2. Fee
sections.body: Owner will pay Performer {{fee}} within 7 days after the session. This is the full payment for the services and rights below, except payments required by a union contract or by law. Union status: {{union_status}}.

sections.title: 3. Rights in the recordings
sections.body: Performer's recorded performances (the "Performances") are works made for hire for Owner to the extent the law allows. To the extent they are not, Performer assigns to Owner all rights in the Performances and the recordings containing them, worldwide, for the full term of copyright. Owner may edit, mix, and use the Performances in any version of the songs, in any media. Performer: [[initial:musician]]

sections.title: 4. Credit and name
sections.body: Owner will make reasonable efforts to credit Performer as "{{musician_alias}} – {{instrument}}" where credits appear. Owner may use Performer's name and approved likeness in credits and promotion of the recordings.

sections.title: 5. Songwriting
sections.body: Performer is not a writer of the songs and has no share of the compositions, unless the writers agree otherwise in a signed split sheet.

sections.title: 6. Songwriting contribution
sections.body: The parties agree Performer contributed to the songwriting. A split sheet signed by all writers will set out Performer's share.

sections.title: 7. Statutory royalties
sections.body: This release does not affect any SoundExchange royalties that non-featured performers receive by law through the AFM & SAG-AFTRA Intellectual Property Rights Distribution Fund.

sections.title: 8. Promises
sections.body: Performer's performances are original and Performer has the right to sign this release, free of conflicting agreements.

sections.title: 9. General terms
sections.body:
- **Whole agreement.** This document (with any attachments named in it) is the parties' entire agreement on its subject and replaces earlier discussions and drafts.
- **Changes.** It can only be changed in a writing signed by all parties.
- **Severability.** If a court finds any part unenforceable, that part is limited to the minimum extent needed and the rest stays in effect.
- **No waiver.** Not enforcing a term once is not a waiver of it later.
- **Notices.** Notices must be in writing and delivered by hand, by a recognized courier, by certified mail, or by email to the addresses in this document (or a later address a party gives in writing). Email notice is effective when sent unless the sender receives a bounce-back.
- **Governing law.** The law of the state of {{governing_state}} governs this agreement, without regard to conflict-of-law rules.
- **Counterparts and electronic signatures.** This agreement may be signed in counterparts and electronically. Each party consents to doing business electronically under the federal E-SIGN Act and the state's version of the Uniform Electronic Transactions Act (or New York's Electronic Signatures and Records Act). An electronic signature has the same effect as a handwritten one.

sections.title: Signatures
sections.body:
By signing below, each party agrees to this document.

**Artist or producer** — {{producer_name}}

[[sig:producer]]

Printed name: [[name:producer]]
Date: [[date:producer]]

**Session performer** — {{musician_name}}

[[sig:musician]]

Printed name: [[name:musician]]
Date: [[date:musician]]

disclaimer: This is a starting template from the Chucksi open contract library. It is not legal advice, and using it does not create an attorney-client relationship. Laws vary by state and change over time. Have a licensed attorney in your state review it before you sign. Music rights are split between the composition (song) and the sound recording (master); royalties also depend on PRO, publisher, distributor and label agreements that this template does not change. An entertainment attorney should review deals involving advances, ownership transfers or long terms.
